extracted.intended_audience: authors and editors preparing manuscripts for AMS journals (also useful to book authors and AMS production staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and editorial standards for preparing and copyediting manuscripts for American Mathematical Society (AMS) journals, covering article structure, typography, mathematics editing, figures/tables, references, and related editorial practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 1. Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the standard elements found in AMS journal articles, including enunciation groupings, figure and table requirements, and reference style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the structural components that AMS expects in submitted articles; authors are encouraged to consult these standards while preparing manuscripts to speed publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 1. The Basics of Copyediting for the AMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental copyediting standards and practices used in the AMS journal production system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on decades of AMS experience and on Ellen Swanson's Mathematics into Type; establishes baseline expectations for copyeditors and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 2. Top Matter, Running Heads, and End Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for the article top matter (title, author information), running heads, and end matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what should appear in front-matter and back-matter elements and how they should be formatted for AMS journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 3. Section and Subsection Heads
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on creating and formatting section and subsection headings within AMS journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conventions for hierarchy, capitalization, and numbering of headers used in AMS production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 4. Enunciations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and formatting rules for enunciations (theorems, propositions, lemmas, corollaries, definitions, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers grouping, numbering, labeling, and typographic treatment of mathematical enunciations as expected by AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 5. Footnotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the use and formatting of footnotes in AMS articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies conventions for content appropriate to footnotes and their typographic presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 6. Lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for creating and formatting lists (numbered, bulleted, nested) in AMS manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides conventions to ensure lists are clear and consistent with AMS styling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 7. Figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure requirements for AMS journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes expected figure formats, captions, labeling, and production considerations for inclusion in AMS publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 8. Tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Table requirements for AMS journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies table formatting, captions, and conventions for presenting tabular data in AMS journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 9. Appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on preparing appendices for AMS journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses placement, numbering, and formatting of appendices and material best suited for appendix sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 10. References
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference style and requirements for AMS journal articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details bibliographic formatting, citation conventions, and reference list organization used by AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 11. Corrigenda and Errata
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and standards for publishing corrigenda and errata in AMS journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains when and how corrections to published material are handled and formatted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 2. Editing and Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial style guidance used throughout the AMS publishing program; useful to both journal and book authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains stylistic conventions and copyediting policies that govern textual and typographic choices across AMS publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 12. Editing Text
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for editing prose and textual elements in AMS manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers grammar, punctuation, spelling conventions, and general prose-level editorial expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter 13. Editing Mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance for editing mathematical content (notation, alignment, display math, inline math, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides policies and conventions for consistent presentation of mathematical expressions and notation in AMS publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A. Functions and Operators Set in Roman Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists functions and operators that should be typeset in roman (upright) type rather than italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a reference for correct typographic treatment of common mathematical functions and operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix B. Some Mathematician Names
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions and recommended spellings for mathematician names that commonly appear in the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps ensure consistent and correct rendering of proper names in AMS publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix C. Common Abbreviations and Latin Expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference for commonly used abbreviations and Latin expressions and their proper formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which abbreviations are acceptable and how Latin phrases should be handled typographically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix D. Nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on nomenclature conventions used in AMS publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers standards for consistent naming and terminology across mathematical writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix E. Variables in Various Fonts and Languages
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how variables should appear when using different fonts or non-Latin languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies expected typographic treatment of symbols and variables across font families and linguistic contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix F. Commonly Confused Words
rubrics_metrics.description: A list and guidance on words commonly confused in English and how to use them correctly in manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for copyeditors and authors to avoid frequent lexical errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix G. Sample Edited Article
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample edited AMS article provided as a reference for authors and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a concrete example illustrating the Guide's conventions in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: General guidance: Use of the Guide and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to refer to the Guide while preparing manuscripts; attention to the standards will help bring articles to publication more quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Guide is the most up-to-date compilation of AMS standards; contact [email protected] with comments or questions. Last revised October 2017.
